statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 futures have been halted since Friday's 21:00Z settlement, so no current price path exists to score. Friday's inside-range close, a sharp leader retracement that the index absorbed, and lower implied volatility keep Tail in the low band.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The single flagged window is the CME Globex reopen from 22:00Z on 27 September, where a rejected Strait of Hormuz plan that Iran has not accepted as final, a 10-year near a 19-year high and a week of oil decline meet the thinnest liquidity of the week.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 6; Iran awaits a formal Hormuz answer ahead of the 22:00Z reopen
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures have not traded since Friday 25 September settled at 21:00Z, so this assessment contains no live price-path evidence and says so explicitly. The newest verified tape is Friday's cash close: the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 daily range and about 0.53% below the 30,770.63 52-week high, while the VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 against a 52-week range of 13.38 to 35.30. The S&P 500 closed at 7,743.41 (+0.51%), the Nasdaq Composite at 27,068.72 (+0.48%) and the Dow at 51,828.62 (+0.93%).

Friday's internals are the clearest evidence against a pathological path. Meta, the week's largest index contributor after its Muse assistant rally, fell about 3.3% to 751.66 on profit-taking and a less optimistic broker tone following a roughly 32% monthly run, and the Nasdaq-100 still closed higher. Delayed latest-session context shows the same rotation elsewhere: MSFT +3.66% and QCOM +3.97% against META -3.33% and INTC -3.45%, six of eight megacaps and six of seven semiconductors higher, megacap dispersion 1.92 points and semiconductor dispersion 2.02 points, with Technology +0.85% against Communication Services -0.58%. A leading name retracing sharply while the index absorbs it is mean reversion working, not the repeated extension after failed retracements that Tail measures. Tail therefore sits at 6.

The macro backdrop is demanding and is carried in Stress at 54. The Federal Reserve raised its target range to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September, its first increase since 2023; H.15 for 24 September shows the 10-year at 5.18%, the 2-year at 4.87% and the 30-year at 5.47%; Friday reporting put the 10-year near 5.23%, the highest in about 19 years; and futures-implied odds of a further October increase are around 64%. Equities absorbed that during a week the Nasdaq Composite still gained roughly 2%. WTI settled Friday at 92.41, down 2.33% on the day and about 7.4% on the week, while Trading Economics shows Brent near 104.

The Middle East thread moved since the previous hour, and it moved marginally toward resolution rather than away from it. Trump said on Saturday that he rejected Iran's seven-day Strait of Hormuz plan, which asked the United States to lift its naval blockade, waive oil sanctions, release about 12 billion dollars in frozen assets and observe a regional ceasefire. On Sunday, Araghchi said Iran had seen only an initial informal reaction and was still waiting for mediators to convey Washington's definitive position before deciding how to proceed. The channel is open rather than closed, which trims the unpriced discontinuity premium carried into the reopen, so Stress eases one point from the previous publication. Reporting cited alongside the rejection says renewed strikes are privately expected only after the November midterms, a deferred rather than imminent vector.

Evidence quality is the main constraint. There is no live NQ price path, and the shared market-context file read this run reports partial collection with its futures and calendar sections unavailable and a payload past the 90-minute freshness bound, so it was used only as delayed latest-session confirmation beside independently verified primary sources. Confidence is 73: the macro, rate, energy, volatility and calendar evidence is complete and verified, while intraday structure is simply unobservable. Dominant mode is normal.

The single flagged window is the CME Globex reopen from 22:00Z on 27 September, where the whole unpriced weekend set clears in the thinnest book of the week. The escalation condition would be an initial gap that extends with shallow or failed retracements while yields, oil and index futures align in one direction; an orderly two-way auction that partly fills the gap inside the first hour would invalidate it. The week beyond this window is dense, with Core PCE and final Q2 GDP on 30 September, ISM Manufacturing on 1 October and payrolls on 2 October.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 01:00Z on Saturday 26 September to 00:00Z on Sunday 27 September, entirely inside the weekend halt that began at Friday's 21:00Z settlement. Published Tail eased from 9 to 6 as Friday's inside-range close and declining implied volatility aged without contradiction, Stress rose from 46 to 55 on the rate and Middle East backdrop, and Confidence drifted from 85 down to 74 as price evidence aged. No hour in the window recorded persistent one-way structure or a failed retracement sequence.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are almost entirely a closed market: CME Globex equity-index futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday 27 September, the twenty-second slot of this forecast. Conditional Tail therefore eases to 5 through the dead hours and rises to 14 at the reopen before easing to 11, where a rejected Strait of Hormuz plan that Iran has not accepted as final, oil down about 7.4% on the week and a 10-year near a 19-year high meet the thinnest liquidity of the week. Stress runs between 52 and 61 on that backdrop and Confidence troughs near 65 before improving as live price discovery resumes. The escalation condition would be an initial gap that extends with shallow or failed retracements alongside aligned cross-assets; an orderly two-way reopening auction would invalidate it.
